title: Mandatory CI Quality Gate Clippy Baseline Cleanup
concrete_capability_transition: Brownie release engineering advances the repository-local mandatory gate from failing at rust_clippy to passing every configured Rust, Node, Brownie guard, and RRP-3 process-loss recovery command while keeping Runtime Release Ready false until release evidence and external workflow constraints close.

strategic_capability_mapping.transition: The release gate now enforces workspace clippy with -D warnings and completes the full repository-local mandatory command suite.
strategic_capability_mapping.relationship: This advances runtime-release-guard-ci without editing GitHub workflows or claiming Release Ready; mandatory local gate success is recorded separately from Runtime Release Ready.

answers.strategic_capabilities: The phase advances headless_autonomous_development by making the mandatory release gate enforce a warning-free Rust workspace baseline before later release evidence can be trusted.
answers.new_capability: A contributor can run cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings successfully, and pnpm release:gate now completes the full configured local mandatory gate.
answers.why_existing_functionality_is_insufficie: Before this phase, the new release gate failed closed at rust_clippy because existing brownie-runtime warnings blocked -D warnings, so the mandatory gate could not exercise downstream release checks.
answers.product_gap_if_skipped: Brownie would retain a nominal release gate that immediately fails on known Rust warning debt, leaving CI hardening unable to distinguish Rust quality debt from later release evidence blockers.
answers.non_duplicative: This phase does not add another release contract or reopen ledger/platform work; it removes the first concrete failure exposed by RRP-8.2 release:gate.
answers.no_new_rpc: Yes. No JSON-RPC method or Runtime protocol surface is added.
answers.no_new_summary: Yes. No user-facing summary/report surface is added; the existing release gate evidence is advanced.
answers.runtime_behavior_change: Build/release behavior changes: the workspace now satisfies clippy -D warnings, and the release gate distinguishes mandatory_gate_passed from runtime_release_ready.
answers.headless_autonomous_contribution: The autonomous release loop can now rely on a passing local mandatory gate and continue toward artifact, supply-chain, cross-platform, soak, governance, and workflow-scope closure without confusing gate success for release readiness.
answers.milestone_progress: RRP-8.3 moves runtime-release-guard-ci from contract-only baseline to a passing repository-local mandatory gate while preserving the remaining external and owner-governed release evidence blockers.

non_goals: scheduler, durable queue, supervisor, SaaS, RBAC, Vault, BDK, or Enterprise admin

reject_when: phase claims Runtime Release Ready or raises maturity without generated release evidence
clippy suppressions are blanket crate-level allows rather than targeted fixes or documented expects
release:gate failure is hidden instead of advancing to the next concrete failing command
runtime-module-decomposition assessment drift is ignored instead of updated from live source metrics
workflow files are modified without workflow-scope credentials or owner-approved equivalent path
license, publish settings, tags, release assets, or signing infrastructure are changed by Runtime automation

guard_engine_change_review.review_intent: RRP-8.3 changes Runtime source files, release-gate evidence semantics, and the guarded module-decomposition assessment. Review must confirm clippy fixes are bounded, targeted expects are narrow and justified, module metrics match live source, pnpm release:gate passes the configured local mandatory suite, workflow hardening remains blocked without workflow scope, and runtime_release_ready stays false.

exit_criteria: cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings passes on the workspace.
pnpm release:gate passes every configured Rust, Node, Brownie guard, and RRP-3 process-loss recovery command.
scripts/release-gate.mjs records mandatory_gate_passed separately from runtime_release_ready and release_ready, keeping Runtime Release Ready false while the release contract remains false.
docs/architecture/runtime-module-decomposition-assessment.json metrics are updated from the live collector after clippy cleanup drift.
runtime_release_ready remains false and direct .github workflow hardening remains blocked_external until workflow-scope credentials or owner-approved equivalent CI hardening exists.
behavior_evidence: cargo test --workspace --all-features passes with stabilized fake-git cleanup assertions.
cargo test -p brownie-tools --lib passes after stabilizing fake-git cleanup assertions.
pnpm release:gate -- --evidence /tmp/brownie-rrp8-3-release-gate-postamend.json passes with mandatory_gate_passed=true, runtime_release_ready=false, and release_ready=false.
pnpm --workspace-root guard:runtime-module-decomposition passes after refreshing live module metrics

accepted_capability: The workspace clippy -D warnings mandatory gate passes.
The repo-local release gate completes the configured Rust, Node, Brownie guard, and RRP-3 recovery command suite.
Release gate evidence distinguishes local mandatory gate success from Runtime Release Ready.
Module-decomposition assessment drift caused by the cleanup is reconciled through guarded live metrics.
behavior_evidence: clippy -D warnings passes for the workspace.
release:gate evidence shows all configured commands passing.
release:gate evidence keeps runtime_release_ready=false and release_ready=false.
runtime-module-decomposition guard validates updated source metrics.
safety_boundary: Rust Runtime remains execution, admission, replay, permission, MCP, workspace mutation, durable state, protocol, and completion authority.
CLI and VSIX remain thin transport/projection clients and cannot grant Runtime authority.
GitHub workflow settings, branch protection, protected tags, signing authority, license choice, and publish posture remain owner-controlled until explicitly provided.
Raw prompt, provider output, file content, absolute/canonical path, secret, environment value, executable content, and process output are not persisted as release evidence.
non_goals: Does not claim Runtime Release Ready.
Does not edit .github workflow files without workflow scope.
Does not generate or publish release artifacts, tags, packages, license metadata, signatures, or release assets.

Does not add hosted scheduler, daemon, durable queue, supervisor, SaaS control plane, customer RBAC, Vault, billing, BDK, Enterprise admin, generic shell, arbitrary process execution, or remote Git capability expansion.
rejected_alternatives: Rejected crate-level clippy allow because the mandatory gate should expose real warning debt.
Rejected marking runtime-release-guard-ci closed because workflow hardening, artifacts, scans, SBOM, checksums, provenance, reviews, and owner-controlled settings remain incomplete.
Rejected editing .github/workflows/ci.yml because the active credentials do not have workflow scope.
technical_debt: runtime-release-guard-ci remains open until repo-local release scripts, permitted CI paths, workflow hardening, artifacts, security scans, cross-platform smoke tests, soak evidence, and governance settings are complete.
Owner license, publish posture, signing or integrity mechanism, branch protection, protected tags, and independent reviews remain required before Runtime Release Ready.
next_capability_rationale: Continue with supply-chain, artifact, cross-platform, soak, and governance release evidence that can be implemented locally, then return to workflow hardening when workflow-scope credentials or owner-approved equivalent path exists.

runtime_release_dod: Closed RRP-1 through RRP-7.2 and RRP-5.18 evidence remains in force and is not reimplemented.
RRP-8.2 establishes the Release Engineering Contract and local gate baseline while keeping runtime_release_ready false.
Missing release artifacts, scans, SBOM, checksums, signatures or integrity proof, provenance, workflow run, tested commit, and independent reviews remain release-blocking.
runtime_boundary_contracts: No new RPC surface is added.
CLI and VSIX remain thin clients over Runtime-owned contracts.
external_control_plane_responsibilities: External scheduling, durable queues, worker leases, hosted isolation, metrics, alerts, SLA, tenant administration, billing, and secret-provider operations remain outside local Runtime v0.
external_adapter_responsibilities: Forge, pull request, review, notification, SIEM, OTel, language verifier, customer integration, and hosted MCP adapter responsibilities remain outside this phase.
commercial_solution_readiness: Packaging publication, license choice, signing authority, notarization, enterprise administration, operational runbooks, support, and commercial release decisions remain owner-controlled or later release work.
Cargo license and publish settings remain owner-decision items and are not changed by RRP-8.2.

technical_debt.next_action: Add remaining repository-local artifact, supply-chain, cross-platform, soak, governance, and permitted CI evidence, then wire mandatory workflow once workflow scope or owner-approved equivalent path exists.
Owner must provide workflow-scope credentials or approve an equivalent CI-hardening path before direct .github workflow gate closure.
Owner must choose license and publish posture before public OSS release; Runtime automation must not change license, publish metadata, release tags, or release assets.

closeout_review.evidence: RRP-8.2 defines the release engineering contract and local gate baseline but does not claim artifact, security, cross-platform, governance, workflow, or owner-setting completion.
